title: Insightec of Tirat Carmel developed a focused ultrasound treatment for essential tremor, with no incision and no implant

trailer.text: Insightec is an Israeli privately held medical device company from Tirat Carmel that sells MR guided focused ultrasound equipment.
It was founded in 1999 on the initiative of Kobi Vortman, a healthcare entrepreneur and expert in medical imaging.
According to the company, its device, Exablate Neuro, targets focused ultrasound waves and ablates tissue deep within the brain, with no incisions and no implants.
In 2016 the FDA approved the device for the treatment of essential tremor.
According to MedCity News, by 2019 about 2,000 tremor patients had been treated with it.

glance.label: Founder
glance.value: Kobi Vortman, and according to Wikipedia also Oded Tamir

stations.title: A tremor that disrupts the day

paragraphs.text: According to Insightec, essential tremor is the most common movement disorder.
According to the company, people with it find it hard to perform everyday tasks, and this impairs their quality of life.
According to MedCity News, there are medications for tremor, but in more severe cases they are largely ineffective.
In such cases the standard of care is deep brain stimulation, a complex surgery to place electrodes near the center of the brain.
According to MDDI, there is also thalamotomy, a riskier surgical approach that destroys part of the thalamus in order to stem the tremor.
Kobi Vortman received a BSc in Electrical Engineering and a PhD in Electro-Optics from the Technion in Haifa.
He established the technology at Elbit Medical Imaging, and from there it led to the founding of Insightec in 1999, in a joint effort by Elbit and GE Healthcare.

According to Wikipedia, Vortman founded the company in 1999 with Oded Tamir, with seed investment from Elbit Medical Imaging and GE Healthcare, but in Wikipedia itself this statement is marked 'citation needed'.
According to Eyal Zadicario, Vortman's vision, that focused ultrasound can transform the lives of millions, was very controversial in the early years.

According to MDDI, at the time the article was published, Insightec, which was privately held, was held by GE Healthcare, Elbit Imaging, York Capital Management, GEOC Hentong Investment Limited Partnership and MediTech Advisors, who by then had together invested $300 million in the company's ultrasound technology.
According to MDDI, the company is based in Israel and has offices in Dallas and Miami.

stations.title: Sound waves that converge on one point

paragraphs.text: According to MedCity News, focused ultrasound concentrates multiple high intensity sound waves using an acoustic lens and targets the energy using medical imaging.
The treatment is performed under MRI guidance, which allows it to be monitored in real time.
According to Maurice Ferré, the company's CEO, to reach the brain the waves must pass through bone, and bone absorbs and diffuses energy.
According to MDDI, when the beams reach the brain they need to align so that they hit only the intended tissue.
According to Ferré, the technology that aligns the beams is similar to the one Israel uses in Iron Dome.
According to MDDI, the procedure lasts three to four hours, and the patient is fully conscious and wears a cooling cap.
According to MDDI, with each 10–15 second pulse, patients may feel headaches, dizziness and numbness in parts of the body.
According to Insightec, the treatment requires a single session with no anesthesia, and patients quickly return to normal activity.
According to MDDI, Insightec studied the technology for three years in a randomized, sham-controlled trial involving 76 patients who did not respond to medication.
According to the company, 56 of them were assigned to treatment and 20 to the sham procedure.
According to Insightec, a year after the procedure the patients retained a 40% improvement compared to baseline.
According to the company, the control group had no improvement, and some experienced a slight worsening.
According to Wikipedia, the trial data were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in the month after the approval.
According to MassDevice, the company applied for pre-market approval in October 2015.
According to MDDI, the FDA granted the approval in July, giving surgeons a completely new approach to treating tremor.
According to Insightec, the approval is for the non-invasive treatment of essential tremor in patients who have not responded to medication.
According to MDDI, the approval requires the company to conduct annual follow-up studies for five years after treatment.
Earlier, in 2004, Exablate was the first focused ultrasound device approved by the FDA for the treatment of uterine fibroids.
According to MedCity News, FDA approval for the treatment of pain from bone cancer came in 2012.
According to Wikipedia, that same year the company received a European CE mark for the treatment of neurological disorders in the brain, including essential tremor.
According to MassDevice, in an article from July 2016, Health Canada approved Exablate Neuro in May of that year.
According to MDDI, the technology also has approval in Korea and Israel.
Dr. Jeffrey Elias said that patients show immediate tremor control and go back to eating and writing.
Ferré said the treatment has enabled patients to enjoy their hobbies or extend their careers.
According to MDDI, in 2016 the company counted about 500 brain procedures at 30 medical centers around the world.
According to MedCity News, in 2019 the device was offered at 16 sites in the U.S.
According to MedCity News, 18 Blue plans in the U.S., equivalent to around 50 million covered lives, cover the treatment, and Medicare covers it in 38 states.
According to MedCity News, the company is likely to tackle neuropathic pain, for which it has received approval in Europe, Russia and Korea.
According to MDDI, in another application ultrasound is used to temporarily open the blood-brain barrier and deliver targeted drugs to the brain.
According to MedCity News, the number of manufacturers in the field has ballooned to nearly 50 companies.
According to the company's website, in 2017 Exablate Neuro won the Prix Galien as best medical technology product.
According to the company's website, in 2018 it won an Edison Award in the medical innovation category.
According to the company's website, that same year Fast Company ranked Insightec the #1 innovative company in the Israel sector.

According to MassDevice, in an article from July 2016, in January of that year Insightec raised $22 million and appointed Maurice Ferré, and Kobi Vortman, the former CEO, stepped down and joined the board.
According to Wikipedia, Ferré is the founder and former CEO of Mako Surgical.
According to MedCity News, he focused on neurology.
According to MedCity News, in 2017 the company raised $150 million in a round led by Koch Disruptive Technologies, at a valuation of $610 million.
According to MedCity News, Ferré hopes to install 300 or more systems in the U.S. over the next decade.
According to the company's website, it has 400 employees.
According to the Focused Ultrasound Foundation, Kobi Vortman himself became a patient when he underwent treatment with the technology for Parkinson's disease.
According to his son, the treatment greatly reduced the tremor and stiffness, and improved his posture and how far he can walk.
According to his son, his physician, Dr. Lior Lev-Tov at Rambam, is interested in innovative treatments.
According to Stryker's announcement, Mako Surgical was acquired for $30 per share, with an aggregate purchase price of approximately $1.65 billion.
Carlos Peña of the FDA said the device is not a cure, but can help patients live better.
According to Practical Neurology, 184 adverse events were reported in the treatment group, 137 of them mild and 46 moderate.
According to Dr. Krishna, focused ultrasound is an alternative to deep brain stimulation, not a replacement, and some patients have skulls that are too thick.
On the other hand, according to MedCity News, focused ultrasound has a low risk of infection or bleeding, and recovery takes hours or days.
According to MedCity News, the equipment costs around $2 million.

According to MedCity News, in the years after the 2004 and 2012 FDA approvals and before Maurice Ferré was appointed CEO, and despite the approvals and investments, reimbursement and a viable American market for the technology did not materialize.
According to MedCity News, one of the reasons for the failure of the company's fibroid product was the lucrative business many providers had in performing hysterectomies.

claims.text: לפי ויקיפדיה, ב-2016 החברה שכרה את מוריס פרה, מייסד ומנכ"ל לשעבר של Mako Surgical, כמנכ"ל.
claims.quote: In 2016, the company hired Maurice R. Ferré, the founder and former CEO of Mako Surgical, as its CEO.

claims.text: לפי MedCity News, ב-2017 החברה גייסה סבב E של 150 מיליון דולר בהובלת Koch Disruptive Technologies בשווי של 610 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: a $150 million Series E round led by Koch Disruptive Technologies in 2017 at a post-money valuation of $610 million.

claims.text: לפי MedCity News, פרה מקווה להתקין 300 מערכות או יותר בארה"ב בעשור הקרוב.
claims.quote: with the hope to install 300 or more systems in the U.S. over the next decade.

claims.text: לפי אתר החברה, לאינסייטק 400 עובדים במשרדים בחיפה, מיאמי, דאלאס, שנגחאי וטוקיו.
claims.quote: 400 strong at offices in Haifa, Israel, Miami, Dallas, Shanghai, and Tokyo

claims.text: לפי קרן האולטרסאונד הממוקד, קובי וורטמן עצמו הפך למטופל.
claims.quote: Now, in a unique turn of events, he has become a patient himself

claims.text: לפי בניו של וורטמן, הטיפול הפחית מאוד רעד וקשיחות והביא לשיפור בתנוחת גופו ובמרחק ההליכה שלו.
claims.quote: He had much less tremors and stiffness, which led to an improvement in his posture and how far he can walk.

claims.text: לפי בניו של וורטמן, הרופא שלו ד"ר ליאור לב-טוב ברמב"ם מעוניין בטיפולים חדשניים.
claims.quote: We were fortunate that his physician, Dr. Lior Lev-Tov at Rambam Hospital, is interested in trying new, innovative treatments.

claims.text: קרלוס פניה מה-FDA אמר שהמכשיר החדש אינו מרפא אך יכול לסייע למטופלים ליהנות מאיכות חיים טובה יותר.
claims.quote: this new device is not a cure but could help patients enjoy a better quality of life.

claims.text: לפי Practical Neurology, בקבוצת Exablate Neuro דווחו 184 אירועים שליליים, מהם 137 קלים ו-46 בינוניים.
claims.quote: 184 adverse events (AEs) were reported in the Exablate Neuro group (137 mild AEs and 46 moderate AEs).

claims.text: לפי ד"ר קרישנה, אולטרסאונד ממוקד הוא חלופה לגירוי מוחי עמוק ולא תחליף, ולחלק מהמטופלים יש גולגולת עבה מדי.
claims.quote: But Krishna added that focused ultrasound offers an alternative to deep brain stimulation, not a replacement. Some patients have skulls too thick for ultrasound.

claims.text: לפי MedCity News, לאולטרסאונד ממוקד סיכון נמוך לזיהום או דימום והחלמה מהירה בהרבה, של שעות או ימים.
claims.quote: Focused ultrasound, on the other hand, has little risk of infection or bleeding and a much faster recovery time of hours or days, rather than weeks.

claims.text: לפי MedCity News, ציוד Exablate Neuro עולה כ-2 מיליון דולר וההליך האמבולטורי נמשך שעתיים עד ארבע.
claims.quote: The cost of the Exablate Neuro equipment is around $2 million and the outpatient procedure takes between two and four hours.

claims.text: לפי MedCity News, למרות האישורים וההשקעות, החזר כספי ושוק אמריקאי בר-קיימא לטכנולוגיה לא התממשו.
claims.quote: But, the approval and investments notwithstanding, reimbursement and a viable U.S. market for the technology failed to materialize.

claims.text: לפי MedCity News, אחת הסיבות לכישלון מוצר הפיברואידים של אינסייטק הייתה הסטטוס קוו: העסק המשתלם של ספקים רבים בביצוע כריתות רחם.
claims.quote: the status quo: the lucrative business many providers had in performing hysterectomies.

claims.text: לפי המכונים הלאומיים לבריאות של ארה"ב, כפי שדווח ב-MDDI, עד 10 מיליון בני אדם בארצות הברית סובלים מרעד חיוני.
claims.quote: According to the National Institutes of Health, as many as 10 million people in the United States suffer from essential tremor

claims.text: לפי ויקיפדיה, מטה החברה נמצא בטירת הכרמל ויש לה משרדים בדאלאס, מיאמי, טוקיו ושנגחאי.
claims.quote: The company is headquartered in Tirat Carmel, and maintains offices in Dallas, Miami, Tokyo, and Shanghai.

claims.text: לפי אינסייטק, מטופלי Exablate Neuro הראו שיפור של כמעט 50% ברעד ובתפקוד המוטורי שלושה חודשים אחרי הטיפול לעומת הבסיס.
claims.quote: Patients treated with the Exablate Neuro showed nearly a 50% improvement in their tremors and motor function three months after treatment compared to their baseline score.

claims.text: לפי Practical Neurology, אחרי שלושה חודשים נרשם שיפור של 46.9% בציון CRST לעומת הבסיס אצל המטופלים.
claims.quote: After 3 months, participants treated with Exablate Neuro showed a 46.9% improvement from baseline in CRST score

claims.text: לפי MedCity News, ב-2018 הרגולטורים הרחיבו את האינדיקציה לפרקינסון עם רעד דומיננטי.
claims.quote: That was followed up with an expanded indication from regulators in 2018 for the treatment of with tremor-dominant

claims.text: לפי Practical Neurology, המכשיר אושר קודם ב-2021 לטיפול בחולי פרקינסון עמיד לתרופות עם בעיות ניידות, קשיחות או דיסקינזיה.
claims.quote: The device was previously approved in 2021 for the treatment of people with drug-refractory Parkinson disease (PD) with mobility, rigidity, or dyskinesia symptoms.

claims.text: לפי הודעת סטרייקר, חברת Mako Surgical נרכשה תמורת 30 דולר למניה, במחיר רכישה כולל של כ-1.65 מיליארד דולר.
claims.quote: for $30.00 per share with an aggregate purchase price of approximately $1.65 billion.
